summary: legal checked in 5 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; keep private. Evidence: Woot API documentation confirms access mechanics only, while current public terms restrict collection, derivative use, and commercial/public reuse of listings, descriptions, and prices. No written permission or API agreement authorizing storage, historical derivation, public display, caching, alerts, affiliate use, or advertising is evidenced. Accuracy/freshness, security, privacy, measurement, attribution, and owner gates also remain incomplete. Exact decision: authorize only bounded read-only evidence work and internal draft preparation; do not expose publicly, expand alerts, send external outreach, change credentials/configuration, deploy, or spend. Human counsel is required before relying on any upstream permission or expanding monetization.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active. Progress: the checklist, official Woot documentation and terms, repository data-flow files, privacy/cookie pages, and draft terms are evidenced. No open launch task is closed because required permission, retention/deletion, consent configuration, vendor/DPA, incident handling, security, accuracy, attribution, measurement, and owner evidence is incomplete. Next evidence actions: attach a field-level rights matrix to a draft Woot permission request; produce the alert-data retention/deletion/access table from repository and deployed configuration; capture deployed consent and GA4 settings; and inventory logs, vendors, and incident/request procedures.

Data-use review dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data—blocked; missing current written permission/API agreement, field-level rights, permitted caching/display/alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, and takedown rules. Smallest next action: draft the permission request and rights matrix without sending it. User alert rules and sync results—evidence_needed; missing data inventory, retention/deletion/access/correction workflow, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior. Smallest next action: produce a read-only data-flow and retention table. GA4 analytics—evidence_needed; missing deployed consent/withdrawal evidence, GA4 property and data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdiction-specific review. Smallest next action: capture the existing consent and GA4 configuration without enabling tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data—evidence_needed; missing log-field inventory, retention/access controls, vendor terms or DPA coverage, and incident/data-request procedures. Smallest next action: produce the operator/vendor inventory from authorized metadata.

Fleet compliance is a technical baseline, not certification: 35 sites pass, 18 fail, and 6 are unknown; open findings include banner, accept/reject consent, GA4, privacy, and terms gaps. These findings require site-specific remediation or evidence before relying on affected sites for a gated launch. Incomplete analytics or revenue telemetry does not by itself block ordinary low-risk growth, but no unsupported revenue, ROI, margin, or causal-lift claims are cleared. Revenue evidence remains partial aggregate: $4.92 is unattributed, while site-attributed income is $0.

Concrete private-site decision: keep SearchWoot private. The launch rule is unmet because every applicable legal data-use item lacks a final disposition, upstream rights are blocked, and technical, security, accuracy, measurement, and owner gates remain blocked. Do not close any launch-readiness task or authorize go-live. No implementation.launch_gate="go_live" or legal_review.status="approved" is supported by the evidence.
